messages:
maya: heads-up: we hit a nasty perf regression on Mistral-7B after exporting with max_position_embeddings=32768. end-to-end p95 increased ~2.1x and the kernel selector is choosing the slow GEMM path for long-prefix workloads.
alex: can you paste the exact export/runtime flags you used? want to see rope scaling and kv settings.
maya: sure — export snippet + runtime flags below:
```
model = {
  \"arch\": \"mistral-7b\",
  \"max_position_embeddings\": 32768,
  \"rope_scaling\": {\"type\": \"linear\", \"factor\": 1.8},
  \"kv_cache_mode\": \"sliding-window\"
}
# runtime: --kernel-policy=auto --batch-timeout-ms=5 --kv-window-size=2048
```
ryan: if the mask builder or rope compute uses absolute positions that will inflate the perceived active context length. kernel estimator likely uses that to compute scratch -> chooses slower kernel. did tracer show where time is going?
maya: short flame summary from tracer (condensed):
```
88% in: attention_mask_expand -> rope_offset_calc -> selector_estimate -> fallback_dense_gemm
Hot spots: mask_expand, rope_offset_calc
```
samir: try enabling mask cache + reduce kv-window to 768 and see if kernel_selector flips back. also try normalizing positions before RoPE compute.
maya: ran a few microbench configs:
- baseline (no maxpos change): p50=26ms p95=58ms
- maxpos=32k, kv-window=2048: p50=61ms p95=170ms
- maxpos=32k, kv-window=768 + --enable-mask-cache: p50=33ms p95=72ms
So mask-cache + smaller kv-window recovers most of the perf, but still not identical to baseline tail.
alex: that points to two contributors: (1) rope_offset_calc doing heavier math at high absolute positions; (2) selector_estimate using raw context_end_pos (or max_position_embeddings) in its scratch estimations. Quick mitigation: map absolute positions to local window indices before performing RoPE math when kv_cache_mode==sliding-window. Should reduce unique offsets and the work in rope_offset_calc.
ryan: agreed. small patch idea:
```
# in build_rope_offsets
if kv_mode == 'sliding-window':
  pos = position % kv_window
else:
  pos = position
# continue with existing rope scale logic
```
This keeps RoPE angles compact and helps selector see smaller effective lengths.
ciara-bot: deploy-bot: CI patch build started for rama/kv-pos-normalize (id: ci-4892).
maya: applied the pos-normalize patch and re-ran the microbench (kv-window=768, mask-cache on). New numbers: p50=28ms p95=60ms. With kv-window=2048 + mask-cache + pos-normalize: p50=36ms p95=95ms.
I also enabled --debug-kernel-selection and grabbed a snippet of kernel_selector.log:
```
[INFO] candidates: {fast_masked_attention, dense_gemm}
[SELECT] fast_masked_attention for effective_kv<=1280
[REJECT] fast_masked_attention for effective_kv>1280 due to est_scratch>gpu_thresh
```
ryan: that confirms the estimator still uses the configured kv_window or absolute length rather than the tile-aligned effective active length. We should: (1) compute effective_kv_length = min(kv_window, observed_active_len) then round up to kernel tile size before scratch calc, and (2) add a tiny mask fingerprint (e.g., 64-bit rolling hash of mask tile pattern) so repeated sliding windows reduce estimated entropy.
samir: I'll open a PR to update the kernel estimator to use tile-aligned effective length + mask-fingerprint caching. I'll include unit tests with Mistral-7B sliding-window + rope-scaling edge cases.
maya: in the short term I'll document mitigation steps for customers: prefer kv_window<=1024 + --enable-mask-cache or deploy the pos-normalize patch until estimator changes land. Also adding a telemetry gauge for mask-fingerprint-cache-hit and an alert if kernel_selector falls back to dense_gemm for >1% of requests in a minute.
alex: good call. can we also add a small perf regression alert tied to increases in rope_offset_calc time-per-token? that will catch similar regressions early.
ryan: ack, adding that to the console dashboards. ping me when samir opens the PR, I'll review estimator math.
ciara-bot: deploy-bot: CI patch build succeeded (ci-4892) 12 merged to rama/kv-pos-normalize.
maya: merging to internal canary now and watching tail latency for the next 2 hours. :eyes:
